# Nebius brings compute pricing into the open as Europe’s AI builders scale on its cloud

October 21, 2026

- Introduces public live prices for GPU spot capacity to expand transparent and flexible access to AI compute
- Expands AI Builder Program to Europe with NVIDIA to accelerate European AI development
- Across countries and industries, Europe’s most ambitious AI companies are building on Nebius

BERLIN — NVIDIA GTC, October 21, 2026 — Nebius (Nasdaq: NBIS), the AI cloud company, today announced public live spot pricing for GPU compute, giving teams greater visibility and control over their compute costs.

AI teams are increasingly experimenting, training and running production services at the same time. Each calls for a different way to access and use compute capacity. Nebius is expanding its portfolio of pricing mechanisms to meet these needs, as part of its vision to promote an open market for compute.

Alongside live preemptible spot pricing, reserve auctions offer defined capacity blocks for short-term compute needs, while pay-as-you-go enables access to compute on demand without a fixed-term reservation. Nebius is also piloting a capacity-rebate program that enables customers to recover value by releasing idle GPUs back into the spot capacity pool.

...

Nebius is working with the ecosystem to make live pricing more widely available. Public live pricing for Spot PVMs is available now at nebius.com/spot-prices and on Shadeform, Silicon Data and GPU Finder.

results.title: Nebius Makes Live Preemptible GPU Prices Public Across Regions | TokenPost
results.author: Simon Yoon
highlights:
On Oct. 21, Nebius announced that customers could publicly view live prices for its preemptible GPU capacity online and through marketplace partners, making rates available by GPU model and region.

The prices are listed on Nebius’ website and through Shadeform, Silicon Data and GPU Finder. A public API provides rates for each GPU and region along with the time each rate takes effect; it does not require an account. The rates describe a specific GPU in a specific location at a particular time, so the effective time is part of the price information.

Nebius announced its dynamic spot-pricing model on Sept. 22, and the model took effect Oct. 8. Rates reflect capacity and demand for each GPU type in each region and may change as often as every 15 minutes. The maximum spot rate is one cent below the current on-demand rate for the same GPU.

A price snapshot at 5:29 a.m. ET (09:29 UTC) on Oct. 21 showed an H200 GPU-hour at $0.886 in us-central1 and $4.49 in eu-west1. The figures show the regional difference at that moment; they are not continuing quotes. A GPU-hour is the listed price for one GPU for one hour, and the snapshot does not establish what a customer would pay later.

Preemptible virtual machines use capacity that has already been allocated but is temporarily idle. That capacity can be reclaimed. Customers can set a maximum price, and an instance stops if the spot rate exceeds the limit, while its data is retained. The service is suited to flexible workloads such as experimentation, data processing and short fine-tuning jobs, where the work can accommodate an interruption.

results.title: Nebius Puts Live GPU Spot Prices in Public: H100 Compute From $0.79 an Hour – PricingRank
highlights:
Nebius Puts Live GPU Spot Prices in Public: H100 Compute From $0.79 an Hour – PricingRank

# Nebius macht Live-Spotpreise für GPUs öffentlich: H100-Computing ab $0.79 pro Stunde

 22/10/2026 

Das Wichtigste: Der KI-Cloud-Anbieter Nebius hat seine GPU-Spotpreise öffentlich gemacht — live, teils alle 15 Minuten aktualisiert — ab $0.79 pro GPU-Stunde für Nvidia-H100- und H200-Chips sowie $0.99 für B200 und B300. Angekündigt am 21. Oktober auf dem GTC-Event von Nvidia in Berlin, macht der Schritt die Kosten für KI-Compute für jeden auf einem öffentlichen Ticker verfolgbar — neben Reserveauktionen, Pay-as-you-go-Zugang und einem Pilotprogramm, das Kunden dafür bezahlt, ungenutzte GPUs in den Spot-Pool zurückzugeben.

## Was sich geändert hat

Nebius, die in Amsterdam ansässige “Neocloud”, die an der Nasdaq als NBIS notiert ist, hat auf der GTC Berlin öffentliche Live-Spotpreise für seine preemptiblen GPU-Kapazitäten vorgestellt. Die Preise werden auf nebius.com/spot-prices sowie über die Marketplace-Partner Shadeform, Silicon Data und GPU Finder veröffentlicht. Das System selbst wurde am 22. September angekündigt und trat am 8. Oktober in Kraft; zuvor sahen Kunden die aktuellen Preise nur in der Nebius-Cloud-Konsole beim Konfigurieren von Ressourcen. Nun sind die Zahlen öffentlich.

| GPU | Spot (ab) | On-Demand | Implizite Ersparnis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nvidia H100 | $0.79 / GPU-Stunde | $4.50 / GPU-Stunde | ~82% |
| Nvidia H200 | $0.79 / GPU-Stunde | $5.40 / GPU-Stunde | ~85% |
| Nvidia B200 | $0.99 / GPU-Stunde | $8.50 / GPU-Stunde | ~88% |
| Nvidia B300 | $0.99 / GPU-Stunde | $9.50 / GPU-Stunde | ~90% |

Die obigen Zahlen sind Starttarife, die The Energy Mag aus den veröffentlichten Nebius-Preisen meldet; sie verstehen sich ohne Steuern und schwanken mit Nachfrage und verfügbarer Kapazität. Maximale Spotpreise sind auf einen Cent unter dem Standard-On-Demand-Preis gedeckelt, und Kunden können bis zu 30 Tage Preisverlauf in der Nebius-Konsole einsehen.

## So funktioniert die Preisbildung

Spotpreise gelten für preemptible VMs mit GPUs. Der Algorithmus von Nebius liest die verfügbare Kapazität und Echtzeit-Nachfragesignale und setzt dann einen Tarif pro GPU-Typ und Region — neu berechnet teils alle 15 Minuten, auch während eine Ressource läuft. Kunden wählen zwischen dem Live-Tarif oder einem Maximalpreis: Ein Maximalpreis ist eine Stoppbedingung, keine Reservierung — steigt der Marktpreis über das Limit, wird der Workload gestoppt. Nebius kann die Kapazität auch komplett zurückfordern. Das Unternehmen beschreibt den Dienst als geeignet für Experimente, Datenverarbeitung und kurzes Modell-Fine-tuning — Workloads, die Unterbrechungen verkraften — statt für dauerhaft laufenden Produktivbetrieb.

Spot ist einer von mehreren Kaufmechanismen, die Nebius im Rahmen dessen ausbaut, was das Unternehmen einen offenen Markt für Compute nennt. Reserveauktionen bieten definierte Kapazitätsblöcke für kurzfristige Bedarfe, Pay-as-you-go ermöglicht On-Demand-Zugang ohne Festzeitreservierung, und ein Capacity-Rebate-Pilotprogramm lässt Kunden Wert zurückgewinnen, indem sie ungenutzte GPUs in den Spot-Pool zurückgeben.

...

Quellen: Nebius-Pressemitteilung via BusinessWire (21. Okt. 2026); The Energy Mag (21. Okt. 2026); btw.media; Nebius-AI-Cloud-Dokumentation.

results.title: Nebius Publishes Live GPU Spot Rates Across Regions and Platforms | EconoTimes
results.author: Elias Mercer
highlights:
Nebius Group N.V. has made live rates for its preemptible GPU capacity public across regions, giving AI cloud customers a way to compare current compute costs before choosing a service that can be interrupted.

On Oct. 21, the company began showing prices on its website and through a public API that requires no account. Shadeform, Silicon Data and GPU Finder also carry the listings. The API supplies the GPU platform, region and effective time for each rate, while Nebius offers up to 30 days of price history.

In an Oct. 21 snapshot taken at 5:29 a.m. ET (09:29 UTC), Nebius listed an H200 GPU-hour at $0.886 in us-central1, versus $4.49 in eu-west1. A GPU-hour is the pricing unit for one GPU used for an hour. Those figures captured listed rates at one moment, rather than prices guaranteed for later use.

Nebius uses demand and spare capacity in a region to set each GPU’s spot rate. It may revise rates every 15 minutes; the highest allowed spot rate for a GPU is $0.01 less than its current on-demand rate. The company announced the dynamic spot model Sept. 22, before it took effect Oct. 8.

The potential savings come with interruption risk. Customers may set a maximum rate, and a virtual machine stops if the spot price exceeds that limit. Nebius can also reclaim the temporarily idle capacity used by the service, making it suited to work that can tolerate a pause.

Nebius says data on attached persistent storage survives an interruption, while data on local solid-state drives does not. Customers may continue paying for retained storage after a machine stops. The public listings give them more information for scheduling flexible work, while the rate and availability can still change during use.

results.title: Nebius launches live spot pricing for GPU compute — TradingView News
highlights:
Nebius launches live spot pricing for GPU compute — TradingView News
# Nebius launches live spot pricing for GPU compute
Nebius NBIS announced Wednesday public live spot pricing for GPU compute, giving teams greater visibility and control over their compute costs.
Shares of NBIS gained nearly 3% pre-market.
The AI cloud company highlighted that public live pricing for Spot PVMs is available now at nebius.com/spot-prices and on Shadeform, Silicon Data, and GPU Finder.
The firm stated that alongside live preemptible spot pricing, reserve auctions offer defined capacity blocks for short-term compute needs, while pay-as-you-go enables access to compute on demand without a fixed-term reservation.
Nebius is also piloting a capacity-rebate program that enables customers to recover value by releasing idle GPUs back into the spot capacity pool.
The AI cloud company said that AI teams are increasingly experimenting, training, and running production services at the same time. Each calls for a different way to access and use compute capacity. Nebius is expanding its portfolio of pricing mechanisms to meet these needs, as part of its vision to promote an open market for compute.
Arkady Volozh, founder and CEO of Nebius, said, “Companies should be able to see what compute costs and access it on terms that fit their work. We are combining that flexibility with the infrastructure, software, and engineering expertise that AI builders in Europe and around the world need to turn ideas into products that can compete globally.”
Additionally, Nebius announced the addition of agentic workflows to its Physical AI Workbench, with customers reporting reductions in engineering time of up to 40%.
The Nebius AI Builder Program is also expanding across Europe with an additional $10 million in compute grants, as well as founder funding opportunities and hands-on community programs.
The company’s education and research arm, Nebius Academy, is collaborating with NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute to launch an education collaboration at GTC Berlin to expand hands-on AI training for developers. Nebius also provides compute grants to support cutting-edge research in AI and AI-driven science.
Nebius and NVIDIA are also collaborating to scale the next generation of hyperscale AI cloud across the full AI technology stack—from AI factory design and deployment to co-building the inference and agentic stack and taking customers into production.
Source: press release
